reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch tie the ages to duty: thirty for transporting the tabernacle, twenty-five for lighter standing service, and twenty once David fixed the sanctuary.

discrepancy.note: Colenso traces the Chronicler drifting from Numbers' thirty-year service age down to twenty, the figure also used in Ezra's day.

quotes.text: at thirtf/ years, as we find it in N.iv.47, (where, probably, we have the rule which prevailed when that Chapter was written,) the writer glides off inadvertently in lCh.xxiii.24,27, to twenty vears, the age at which they were fit for service in Ezra's time, Kzr iii.8, when only 341 above that age returned to Jerusalem.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. V (1865), sec. 267, on Numbers 4:3 and Ezra 3:8.

sides.snippet: from thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all who enter into the service, to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
sides.verseText: from thirty years old and upward even until fifty years old, all who enter into the service, to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
